Dataverse._ClientSecret_comment: REMOVED 2026-08-24 (spaarke-auth-v4-dataverse-MI task 033, ADR-028 A4). Dataverse:ClientSecret is gone: it had ZERO consumers in src/ after task 022 moved every confidential client onto OrderedCredentialClientProvider. THE PREVIOUS TEXT HERE WAS FALSE AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REINTRODUCED: it read 'WARNING: DO NOT remove the secret backing this setting - the shared-lib Dataverse path STILL hard-requires it; removing it from Key Vault CRASHES the BFF at startup.' That was true when written (2026-08-13) and was invalidated by tasks 022 (migrated the call sites) and 024 (relaxed DataverseOptions.cs:32 [Required]+ValidateOnStart). It was never refreshed, so it went on instructing operators not to do the very thing this project exists to do - the same failure mode as .claude/constraints/auth.md:108, which made three prior audits conclude the secret was permanent. Verified empirically 2026-08-24: both Key Vault copies deleted and all four secret app settings removed, BFF healthy, OBO green including a byte-exact SPE round-trip. Dataverse is reached under the user-assigned managed identity mi-bff-api-{env} (dev clientId 5967251e-171c-46fe-a6c2-ef843c90309d) app-only, or under the calling user via OBO on the MI-FIC assertion. Register the UAMI as the Dataverse Application User.

Graph._ManagedIdentity_comment: When Enabled=true, GraphClientFactory.CreateAppOnlyClient() uses DefaultAzureCredential (App Service managed identity). Set ClientId when using a User-Assigned MI; leave null for system-assigned. Per-tenant container-type configs in SpeAdminGraphService are unaffected — they use per-customer owning-app secrets from Key Vault (ADR-028 exception E-1). Operator action before deploying with Enabled=true: grant the MI service principal the same Microsoft Graph application permissions previously held by the BFF app registration (FileStorageContainer.Selected, Files.Read.All, etc.). CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (task 033): this comment used to end 'OBO flow (per-user) is unaffected — still uses API_CLIENT_SECRET via ConfidentialClientApplication.' That is no longer true and is the single sentence-shape this project exists to eliminate. OBO now runs on a Managed-Identity-issued federated credential too — see Graph:Credentials below. Three prior audits concluded the secret could never be removed on the strength of a sentence like this one.
Graph._Credentials_comment: ADR-028 A4 — how the BFF proves it is a confidential client, INCLUDING on the OBO (delegated) path. Order is evaluated first-to-last. The canonical default is [ManagedIdentityFederated, ClientSecret] and is applied ONLY when this section is absent, because the configuration binder MERGES into an existing collection — so an operator narrowing the order to [ManagedIdentityFederated] gets exactly that, and does not silently get a trailing ClientSecret back. RequireSecretFreeIdentity=true makes the app REFUSE TO START outside Development if ClientSecret is still listed: a secret sitting beneath the federated credential is worse than no migration, because a broken MI-FIC would fall through to it silently while every health signal stayed green. Development is exempt — a workstation has no route to IMDS.

DocumentIntelligence._ModelTier_comment: ai-advanced-capabilities-nda-r1 task 010: per-Action model-tier deployment routing (ADR-016). BingSearch._comment: AUTH (auth-v4 task 056 / FR-E7): Bing is genuinely third-party with no Entra option, so the KEY STAYS (ADR-028 Group 1 carve-out) - only its RESOLUTION changed. WebSearchHandler prefers ApiKeySecretName (the LlamaParseClient indirection: this names the config key that carries the value) and falls back to the direct ApiKey setting. NOTE the honest limitation: neither form keeps the value out of IConfiguration, because App Service resolves a Key Vault reference INTO configuration at startup either way; the indirection only makes the secret NAME per-environment. UseMockResults is an EXPLICIT opt-in for sample results when no key is configured - it defaults false because the previous behaviour returned fabricated search results, with real-looking URLs and no degradation note, wrapped as web citations. Guarded by tests/Spaarke.ArchTests/FabricatedResultGuardTests.cs.

_AiSearch_comment: AUTH (auth-v4 task 053 / FR-E4, 2026-08-22): all AI Search clients select their credential in ONE place, Infrastructure/Auth/SearchClientFactory - Entra bearer when AiSearch:ManagedIdentity:Enabled=true OR no admin key is configured, otherwise the admin key. PREREQUISITE: Entra auth is OFF by default on an Azure AI Search service. A service with authOptions=apiKeyOnly returns HTTP 403 to every bearer token REGARDLESS of role assignments, so a Search Index Data Reader/Contributor grant on such a service is inert. Set the service to aadOrApiKey first (az search service update --auth-options aadOrApiKey), which allows both and is reversible. spaarke-search-dev was switched on 2026-08-22. Roles: Search Index Data Reader to read documents, Search Index Data Contributor to index; subscription Owner grants NEITHER (both are dataActions and Owner carries none). The dead ApiKeySecretName property was removed - it was bound and read by nothing; the real key reaches consumers via DocumentIntelligence:AiSearchKey, AiSearch:ReferencesApiKey and RecordSync:AiSearchApiKey.

AiSearch._AllowedIndexes_comment: Multi-container-multi-index-r1 (Phase B, FR-BFF-06): allow-list of physical AI Search index names that callers may target via the per-record / per-request searchIndexName parameter on IKnowledgeDeploymentService.GetSearchClientAsync. Requests specifying an indexName NOT in this list MUST be rejected by the resolver with ProblemDetails 400 + stable error code INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED (ADR-019 + NFR-08). Empty array means no caller-supplied indexes accepted (the 2-tier Dataverse → appsettings fallback still applies when indexName is omitted).

AiSafety._ContentSafety_comment: Safety perimeter (AIPU2-020/021): Content Safety APIs (text:shieldPrompt for PromptShieldService, text:detectGroundedness for GroundednessCheckService) via the named 'ContentSafety' HttpClient. AUTH: MANAGED IDENTITY ONLY (ADR-028 / spaarke-auth-v4-dataverse-MI FR-E1, 2026-08-21). The ApiKey setting was REMOVED: it referenced Key Vault secret 'ContentSafety-ApiKey', which does not exist in the vault the BFF actually uses (spaarke-spekvcert), and no ContentSafety-kind account exists in ANY Spaarke subscription. An unresolvable Key Vault reference is worse than an absent setting here, because ContentSafetyAuthHandler selects the key branch on a NON-EMPTY value. Content Safety is served by the multi-service AIServices account (dev: spaarke-openai-dev), so CONTENT_SAFETY_RESOURCE_NAME resolves to that account, not to a dedicated resource. Operator prerequisite: the App Service managed identity needs 'Cognitive Services User' on that account (dataActions Microsoft.CognitiveServices/* covers accounts/ContentSafety/text:shieldprompt/action); 'Cognitive Services OpenAI User' does NOT cover it. Verified present for the dev UAMI 2026-08-21. WARNING: auth being correct is not sufficient. Over the full 90-day App Insights retention window, dev recorded 122 Prompt Shield scans and ZERO completions - every one hit the 100ms PromptShieldService deadline and failed OPEN. Token acquisition is not the cause (DefaultAzureCredential.GetToken averages 7ms, p95 1ms); the shieldPrompt call itself does not answer inside the budget. Check scripts/kql/ai-metering/shield-coverage.kql BEFORE trusting this perimeter in any environment.

PromptShield._ChatPipelineEnabled_comment: F-8 (audit finding follow-up): wires PromptShieldChatMiddleware onto the LIVE interactive chat pipeline — a PRE-LLM prompt-injection perimeter (hard block on detection) PLUS the per-turn fail-open verdict that feeds the confirmation gate's overlay-2 (SafetyPerimeterDegraded → gated WRITES require confirmation; reads/drafts stay fail-open). DEFAULT false = feature OFF = byte-identical to today (no scan, no block, gate probe unfed). Set true ONLY AFTER the AiSafety:ContentSafety endpoint + auth are configured AND the App Service managed identity holds 'Cognitive Services User' on the Content Safety resource (same grant as the ContentSafety comment above) — otherwise every scan fails OPEN and every gated WRITE degrades to confirm-required (safe direction, but noisy; watch ai.safety.shield_evaluations outcome=failed_open_*). Adds up to ~100ms pre-first-token latency per turn (PromptShieldService hard deadline; NO new timeout is introduced).

Communication._WebhookSigningKey_comment: Task 044: HMAC-SHA256 signing key for /api/communications/incoming-webhook (X-Hub-Signature-256 header). Used when a signing relay (Logic App / Function / APIM) sits in front of the endpoint and signs Graph notifications on Graph's behalf, since Graph itself does not sign bodies. Together with the in-body clientState check, this provides defense-in-depth. Rotate on incident or every 90 days. Filter is fail-closed.
Communication._AutoFile_comment: Task 015 (FR-11 / ADR-018): Association-Engine auto-file kill-switch. 'Enabled'=true auto-files DETERMINISTIC (rungs 0-3) matches at/above 'Threshold' to Resolved; false downgrades them to Suggested (suggest-only) with no redeploy (read via IOptionsMonitor). AI rungs (4-5) NEVER auto-file regardless. 'Threshold' (default 0.85) is tunable up (conservative) or down (aggressive auto-routing). 'Tenants' optionally overrides Enabled/Threshold per opaque tenant key on multi-tenant deployments; omit for single-org. ADR Tension Path A owner override of design DEC-4 — misfile is re-file (audited), never delete.
Communication._SemanticMatch_comment: Task 030 (FR-14): Association-Engine rung 4 (semantic record match over spaarke-records-index via the IRecordMatchingAi facade). 'Enabled'=true (default) runs the rung when the deterministic rungs (0-3) did not auto-file; false makes it a no-op with no redeploy. Rung 4 NEVER auto-files (mapper-enforced) — its candidates surface as Suggested. 'ScoreCeiling' (0.80) keeps semantic confidence below the 0.85 auto-file threshold; 'MinScore' (0.50) drops weak hits; 'Limit'/'MaxCandidates' bound the search fan-out and emitted candidates.
Communication._AiClassification_comment: Task 031 (FR-15): Association-Engine rung 5 (LLM extract+classify via the ICommunicationClassificationAi facade → IOpenAiClient structured output). 'Enabled'=true (default) runs the rung when the deterministic rungs (0-3) AND the semantic rung (4) did not auto-file; false makes it a no-op with no redeploy. Rung 5 emits METADATA-ONLY signals (category/obligations/rationale) and resolves NO regarding target, so it NEVER auto-files and never forces a regarding write — its value is the W5 triage substrate (task 053). Privilege is flagged as a signal only (ADR-015). 'MaxCandidateTypes' (5) bounds the candidate record TYPES reflected into provenance; 'MaxInputChars' (8000) caps the subject+body sent to the model (ADR-016 budget).

TodoGeneration._EnableEventSourcedGeneration_comment: smart-todo-r5 INBOUND fix (2026-08-17, Option A gated). Rules 1 (overdue events) & 3 (deadline proximity) of the nightly TodoGenerationService read sprk_event and were silently producing ZERO To Dos because they routed through the composite IDataverseService whose QueryEventsAsync is a silent-empty stub; they now query via IEventDataverseService (real impl). This flag GATES creation: false (default) = DRY-RUN — the rules query real events and LOG how many To Dos they WOULD create (search app logs for 'TodoGeneration Rule 1 [dry-run]' / 'Rule 3 [dry-run]') so an operator can validate first-run volume, the same-name dedupe, and notification side-effects BEFORE enabling. Set true to create for real. See projects/smart-todo-r5/notes/INBOUND-event-sourced-todo-generation-broken.md (DEF-1, Epic #427). Rules 2/4/5 (budget/invoice/task) are unaffected by this flag.
